doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Tierney Sutton trio
summary: Laws describes the cooperative trio with Tierney Sutton and Larry Koontz and how Kenny Burrell introduced them.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So you seem to have the focus on your projects with your family, and then you’re working – like I said, I saw you with Chick come through the new Yoshi’s, San Francisco, a couple years ago. It sounds like – now, Tierney Sutton. Are you working in her group?
The trio. No, it’s a trio. It’s a cooperative trio. Larry Koontz on guitar and the vocal and flute, which is a very, very unique situation I like a lot.
It must be easy to travel, too.

Yeah, it’s wonderful. It’s just a wonderful ensemble. I like the exposure and the color that we get together. I played – I sat in with them when they played the other night in the Philippines, because they were there too. We played two nights. They played two

nights, but not the same nights. So she invited me to play with them the night before we left. I sat in, played a couple of tunes with them, which she loves, because she likes that combination, flute and vocal. Kenny Burrell was responsible for us meeting, in the sense that he had me come play a duet for the Grammy pre- – Grammy museum, pre-Grammy awards, two years ago. That’s when she was there with Alan Bergman. You know the guy?

She was doing one of Michel Legrand’s tunes. I said, “Boy, that would be nice. Let me sit in with you guys.” She said, “Oh yeah.” So we ended up playing together. From then on, she said wow. So we’ve done gigs. We did The Anthology down there in San Diego, and we did Yakima, Washington. We did UCLA twice, and we did the Grammy museum. So we’re already playing. Now we’re getting ready to do Tempe, Arizona, on the – yeah, like I told you, that conflict I had. That is going to be on the 15th of April.
